skills/_shared/idea-refinement-criteria.md:97:Example: "The external API supports batch operations" — if it doesn't, the entire design around bulk processing doesn't work.
agents/code-reviewer.md:63:Every instruction file enters your context now, before evidence. Keep a loading ledger of absolute paths and mark entries loaded only after contents return; emit a compact completed loading checkpoint. Do not batch source reads with instruction reads. If any instruction read fails, stop and surface the error — do not proceed with partial methodology.
agents/code-reviewer.md:77:- **Large diff (>500 lines)**: Summarize by file first, then review in batches by module/feature area.
skills/review-code/review-process.md:30:A large diff (>500 lines) needs focused batching, not an early content dump. A feature-directory listing may locate task documents; their detailed reading belongs to investigation.
skills/review-code/review-process.md:36:Batch the Known-profile reads together when supported, then reconcile expected paths with completed lookups. Record each rule's match/non-match or the shared procedure's explicit unavailable-file outcome; apply that procedure's ENOENT and root-resolution fallbacks. A skipped lookup leaves routing incomplete even when a file extension suggests an obvious profile. This prevents an assumed negative from hiding an additional applicable profile.
skills/review-code/review-process.md:44:Read each selected `profiles/<profile>/review-code/<checklist>` using the resolved absolute plugin root. An index read is routing, not checklist loading: every selected link requires its own returned file content, even for a tiny diff. Keep the resolved paths as a loading ledger and mark them loaded only when their read results arrive. Do not batch investigation commands with these reads.

skills/review-code/review-isolated.md:43:This is the single entry point for subject-matter investigation. Read the selected full diff and changed files at the reviewed candidate, accounting for deletions. For staged review use index blobs; for a commit range use the selected candidate revision. Materialize those candidate sources outside the worktree when its current files differ; never pass unrelated worktree bytes as reviewed source. Large diffs (>500 lines) may be batched by module; report any context limit.

profiles/k8s/document/rubric.md:67:  - **CPU (compressible).** Exceeding the request causes throttling, not kill. Three patterns are common and all legitimate — state which one applies and why: (a) `requests == limits` for latency-sensitive workloads (Guaranteed QoS; avoids throttling-induced jitter), (b) request set, limit omitted (rely on namespace `LimitRange` or `ResourceQuota`; common for batch/IO-bound workloads where throttling is benign), (c) neither set (BestEffort; batch only, no prioritization guarantees).
profiles/k8s/review-code/finops-checklist.md:55:- **`batch` and `memory_limiter` processors.** The `memory_limiter` processor prevents the Collector from OOMKilling under high load; `batch` processor reduces export API call volume (and therefore cost for pay-per-request backends). A pipeline without `memory_limiter` risks node OOM; a pipeline without `batch` pays per-event API costs. Flag the absence of either as P2.
profiles/k8s/review-code/finops-checklist.md:77:- **PVC `reclaimPolicy: Retain`.** PVs with `Retain` survive PVC deletion — the disk persists in the cloud provider and continues to be billed until manually deleted. This is the correct choice for data you must preserve, but flag it as a P3 finding when the workload is ephemeral or disposable (CI runners, batch jobs, pre-prod environments).
profiles/k8s/review-code/reliability-checklist.md:55:- `revisionHistoryLimit` set to a small-but-useful number (3–10); the default (10) is fine. `revisionHistoryLimit: 0` disables `kubectl rollout undo` entirely and removes the ReplicaSet history that tools like Argo CD use for rollback/diff — flag as P2 unless the workload is ephemeral (CI runner, batch job) or an alternative rollback mechanism is documented.

profiles/js_ts/implement/gotchas.md:22:- Choose batch failure semantics deliberately. `Promise.all` rejects when an input rejects; it does not cancel work already started. Use `allSettled` when all outcomes must be observed, whether for partial success or cleanup before propagating failure, and inspect rejected outcomes. See [Promise aggregation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Promise/all).
